segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Can I ask you this, Jacques, just coming back to Gilbert for a moment? Is it possible that Gilbert was being played — that he was shown something that was an intention to try and see what a master remote viewer would think of what he was being shown?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: He is one of the best psychics in the world today, and has been throughout his career. I met him when he was 22.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What state was the facility he was taken to located in? Did he give you that indication?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I don't know the level — if there is a security wrapper around this, I don't know at what level. So I've purposely been vague in the book.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Was there a date for the encounter? I think you indicated to me earlier it was about 20 years ago. Is that right?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Have you seen any evidence proving that Gilbert was actually at that location? Has he provided you with any substantiation or corroboration?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No. And that's why I don't want to go beyond reporting that conversation and my trust in the conversation. I had no way of checking this. Then my own experience would indicate that that kind of thing is happening, probably.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Can I ask you a few questions, though, and you don't have to answer these if you're uncomfortable. Did he physically touch the entity?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Was the entity a prisoner?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No. I asked him that question, of course. He said the entity was a volunteer.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: You intriguingly talk in your diary about captured or volunteer beings. You're clear that this being was there voluntarily. But it suggests that there are other beings that are captured. How long had the entity been there?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I'm not fudging here, I really don't know the answer.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you know from Gilbert how long the entity had been at this facility, with the humans?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No. I asked Gilbert that, and he did not know: he was there just for that one presentation.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Was the entity alive, in the sense that we think of something being biologically alive?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes. Now, I have no doubt — I'm not an expert about Hollywood, but I've occasionally seen what Hollywood could do in terms of special effects, and of course everything can be a special effect.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did Gilbert explain why he, a remote viewer, was required to communicate with the being if, as you say in the diary, it was communicating with light?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Because the people in charge were smart enough to understand that the communication that being was capable of was beyond… Well, we have the same thing with whales. Whales can read the inside of your body. I mean, women who were attending to whales knew that the whale would know they were pregnant before they knew they were pregnant. So those situations — we have aliens here on Earth in the form of very intelligent animals that perceive things completely outside our range. So it's not a new situation.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: No, but I think this is one of the most important revelations in your latest book: that we are talking here about someone who you accept is telling the truth, who says they were part of what sounds like a US government, US military program where they were asked to communicate with a non-human being. Can I ask you this, sir: did conventional spoken language fail, or was it not possible with this being?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The answers were in the form of light configurations.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And so, had humans learned how to communicate with it through light?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: From what he told me, there was limited knowledge of what was positive and negative. He was asked to only frame questions in a way where the answer could be yes or no. And that's why there were situations where he said he couldn't understand the answer.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: One of the things you say in your diary — and I've learned to read Jacques Vallée's diaries very, very closely indeed — you say Gilbert's answers matched earlier results. Earlier results from whom, Jacques? I really think this is a very important question. What are you talking about there?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: My understanding is that there were teams there that had been working with that being, and perhaps other beings, for a while. I mean, this isn't just a one-off situation, they had a base. Again, I said: what were the insignias? He said there were probably people from different branches of the armed forces there. The people there were experts, men and women, who seemed to be coming and going. There may have been other labs; he was in one lab.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Is it your understanding that this communication with this being is happening today? Is it still happening?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I have no way of knowing.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So it was happening 20 years ago, but we don't know if that program is still operating today.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: What was important to me, again in terms of what we can derive from the database and from all the other contact cases, is that the communication was primarily a form of light.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So Jacques, one of the things you say in the diary is that Gilbert shared with you the actual questions he was asked to put to the being. What was the most important question that he was asked to ask?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I think he should answer that. I would have to make up an answer from what I know. I cannot put my finger on one.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: To come at this another way: what was the most important answer that Gilbert said he got from the being?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I think the most important was that there was a willingness — but I couldn't tell you whether that was from the being itself or from the officers who had briefed him ahead of time — there was a willingness to communicate, that it wanted to establish communication with us.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: That's very exciting, and I think one of the things you also plant in the book is quite a bombshell. You wrote that what Gilbert learned about the goals of the UFO intrusion may be the most insightful part of the entire episode. Can you tell me, sir, what did he learn about the UFO intrusion's goals?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I think he would say that it was coincident with our having access to space: that humanity as we know it is at a point of transition that is critical, where we can just as easily destroy ourselves as a result of it. I can tell you what my emotions are. I entered science because of conversations with my parents. They had lived through two world wars, and our family emerged first being very lucky to be alive, and also thinking that this could not happen again, and that mankind would change. And there was a tremendous outpouring of emotion about the United Nations: the League of Nations had collapsed, but everybody was hopeful something could happen with the UN, and there would never be another world war, because now it was impossible with the atom bomb. It was impossible. And to me, in astronomy — and I think I speak for many of my colleagues — the sky was pure, the sky was open, and this was something we would need everybody to go to. And today we have a thousand classified projects, all aimed at destroying the other guy's satellite, and who is going to get to the Moon first, and are they going to claim the Moon? I mean, there was a treaty that nobody would claim the Moon. China never signed it, and that treaty has expired. So if you want to go claim the Moon, it's up to you.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: I want to come back to your reference to what Gilbert learned about the goals of the UFO intrusion, and how it was the most insightful part of what he told you. Can you at least tell us: were those goals that he described benign, hostile, or neither?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Well, with what we know of the technology — and today we know a lot more than we did five years ago, 15 years ago — there would be no defense, essentially. It can appear at will at any point of the world with very, very large equipment.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Sorry, Jacques, just to clarify: I'm asking about what Gilbert's impressions were about the motivations for the beings making these intrusions to our planet. Was he suggesting that they were benevolently motivated, or hostile?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: To my knowledge, at least within his experience, they never got to a point of clarifying those motivations. The presence of the being, and the fact that that being was cooperating, indicates that on their side there was a willingness and a desire to establish a relationship. I think that's all.
